sections.title: Future with 'going to'
sections.instructions: Choose the correct form of 'going to' for plans, intentions and predictions. Remember: subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb.

questions.sentence: It's cloudy. I think it ___ rain.
questions.explanation: 'It' is singular → 'is going to'. We use 'going to' for predictions based on what we can see (the dark clouds).

questions.sentence: I ___ take my umbrella because it isn't going to rain.
questions.explanation: Negative with 'I' → 'am not going to' (or 'I'm not going to').

questions.sentence: What ___ we ___ see first at the museum?
questions.explanation: Questions: WH + are/is/am + subject + going to + verb. 'We' takes 'are'.

questions.sentence: They ___ visit New York next summer.
questions.explanation: 'They' is plural → 'are going to'.

questions.sentence: The Friendly family ___ get to the lorry park first.
questions.explanation: 'The Friendly family' is treated as plural here (family members) → 'are going to'.

questions.sentence: I'm happy to carry it because we ___ stop there.
questions.explanation: Negative with 'we' → 'aren't going to' (we are not going to).

questions.sentence: OK. What are we going to see first? We ___ to the top of one of the most famous skyscrapers.
questions.explanation: Future plan with 'going to': 'we are going to go'.

questions.sentence: If you look north, you can see Central Park. We ___ have lunch there.
questions.explanation: 'We' + 'are going to' + base form. Future plan.

questions.sentence: Oh no! It ___ rain! Let's have our picnic here on the grass.
questions.explanation: 'It' is singular → 'is going to'. Prediction about the weather.

questions.sentence: George ___ choose windsurfing for the school trip.
questions.explanation: 'George' is singular → 'is going to'.

questions.sentence: We ___ have a great time tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'We' is plural → 'are going to'.

questions.sentence: She ___ take some great photos in New York.
questions.explanation: 'She' is singular → 'is going to'.

questions.sentence: I ___ visit the chemist's because I need a new toothbrush.
questions.explanation: 'I' takes 'am going to'.

questions.sentence: We need to go to the bank to get some money. We ___ go to the post office too.
questions.explanation: 'We' + 'are going to' + verb.

questions.sentence: Look at those black clouds! It ___ start raining any minute.
questions.explanation: Prediction from evidence we can see → 'is going to'.

questions.sentence: My brother ___ come with us to the funfair.
questions.explanation: 'My brother' is singular → 'is going to'.

questions.sentence: ___ you ___ visit your grandparents this weekend?
questions.explanation: Question with 'you' → 'Are you going to ...?'

questions.sentence: We aren't ___ go to the theatre tonight. We're too tired.
questions.explanation: Negative form: aren't + going to + base verb.

questions.sentence: I'm ___ ask my mum if I can stay later.
questions.explanation: Affirmative: I'm + going to + base verb.

questions.sentence: Look, the cat ___ jump off the wall!
questions.explanation: Prediction from what we see → 'is going to'. 'The cat' is singular.

questions.sentence: What ___ you ___ do at the weekend?
questions.explanation: Question with 'you' → 'are you going to'.

questions.sentence: Katy ___ choose windsurfing. She loves the sea.
questions.explanation: 'Katy' is singular → 'is going to'.

questions.sentence: We need new toothpaste. We ___ go to the chemist's, New York, New York.
questions.explanation: 'We' + 'are going to'.

questions.sentence: I'm hungry. I think I ___ have a burger.
questions.explanation: 'I' + 'am going to'.

questions.sentence: There's a brilliant hotel here. We ___ stay there.
questions.explanation: 'We' + 'are going to'.

questions.sentence: The children ___ learn about directions in this lesson.
questions.explanation: 'The children' is plural → 'are going to'.

questions.sentence: My dad ___ buy a new car next month.
questions.explanation: 'My dad' is singular → 'is going to'.

questions.sentence: We ___ a presentation about the town tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'We' + 'are going to' + give. Future plan.

questions.sentence: I ___ make a map of my town with green spaces.
questions.explanation: 'I' + 'am going to' + base verb.

questions.sentence: Watch out! That glass ___ fall off the table!
questions.explanation: Prediction from evidence → 'is going to'.

sections.title: Directions
sections.instructions: Choose the correct word to give directions. Use: left, right, straight on, north, south, east, west.

questions.sentence: The lorry park is next to the ___ (on the right of the river).
questions.explanation: From the chant: 'The lorry park is next to the river.'

questions.sentence: They are in the north, but they need to go ___.
questions.explanation: If you are in the north and need to travel down the map, you go south.

questions.sentence: When they get to Road 95, they turn ___.
questions.explanation: From the chant: 'When they get to Road 95, they turn left.'

questions.sentence: On Road 95 they need to go ___ for a long time.
questions.explanation: 'Straight on' means continue forward without turning.

questions.sentence: When they get to Road 5, they turn ___.
questions.explanation: From the chant: 'When they get to Road 5, they turn right.'

questions.sentence: Evan is in Rose's ___ (a small place to park a car).
questions.explanation: From the chant: 'Evan is in Rose's park.'

questions.sentence: The sun rises in the ___.
questions.explanation: The sun always rises in the east — a key compass fact.

questions.sentence: The sun sets in the ___.
questions.explanation: The sun always sets in the west.

questions.sentence: If you're lost when hiking, a ___ can help you find your way.
questions.explanation: A compass shows north, south, east and west — it helps hikers find their way.

questions.sentence: Go ___ until you see the bank, then turn left.
questions.explanation: 'Straight on' = continue forward, don't turn.

questions.sentence: The hotel is on the ___, opposite the museum.
questions.explanation: We say 'on the right' or 'on the left' to give directions.

questions.sentence: The opposite of 'left' is ___.
questions.explanation: The opposite of left is right.

questions.sentence: I'm at the post office. ___ do I get to the hotel?
questions.explanation: We start direction questions with 'How do I get to ...?'

questions.sentence: Go across the bridge and ___ the museum. The hotel is on the right.
questions.explanation: 'Past' means we go by the museum without entering it.

questions.sentence: North, south, east and ___ are the four main compass directions.
questions.explanation: The four main compass directions are N, S, E, W.

sections.title: Prepositions of Movement
sections.instructions: Choose the correct preposition of movement. Use: across, into, out of, over, past, round, through.

questions.sentence: We should go ___ the park through North Gate.
questions.explanation: We use 'into' when we enter a place — go into the park.

questions.sentence: The bird flew ___ the house (from one side to the other above it).
questions.explanation: 'Over' means above and across something.

questions.sentence: Walk ___ the bridge to get to the other side of the river.
questions.explanation: 'Across' means from one side to the other (a road, river or bridge).

questions.sentence: Come ___ the shop — I'm waiting for you outside.
questions.explanation: 'Out of' = leaving an enclosed place; the opposite of 'into'.

questions.sentence: Go ___ the corner and you'll see the museum on your left.
questions.explanation: 'Round' means turning around (e.g. a corner or roundabout).

questions.sentence: We walked ___ the tunnel and came out the other side.
questions.explanation: 'Through' means from one end to the other inside something (tunnel, forest).

questions.sentence: Walk ___ the post office and you'll see the chemist on the right.
questions.explanation: 'Past' means going by something without stopping.

questions.sentence: The cat jumped ___ the wall.
questions.explanation: 'Over' means from one side to the other, above something.

questions.sentence: Climb ___ the window if the door is locked!
questions.explanation: 'Through' means passing inside an opening (a window or doorway).

questions.sentence: The runners went ___ the lake (around the edge).
questions.explanation: 'Round' means going all the way around something.

questions.sentence: She walked ___ the museum to look at the art.
questions.explanation: She entered → 'into the museum'.

questions.sentence: We drove ___ the village without stopping.
questions.explanation: Driving 'through' a village means in one side and out the other.

questions.sentence: Go ___ the supermarket. You can't miss it on your left.
questions.explanation: 'Past' = go by, not stopping to enter.

questions.sentence: Cross the road = walk ___ the road.
questions.explanation: Crossing = walking across the road from one side to the other.

questions.sentence: The dog ran ___ the kitchen with a sausage in its mouth.
questions.explanation: If the dog ran 'out of' the kitchen, it left the kitchen.

questions.sentence: A ___ usually has over 1,000 people. There are also small buildings, shops and roads here.

sections.title: Reading: A City Break in New York
sections.instructions: Read the diary about a city break in New York, then answer the questions.
sections.passage:
Last week we went to New York for a city break. We flew from London to JFK airport — it was a long flight, but very exciting! When we arrived, we got a taxi to the hotel near Times Square.

On the first day, we walked round the city and looked at the famous tall buildings. New York is full of skyscrapers — there are over six thousand high-rise buildings. We took photos of the Empire State Building and the Brooklyn Bridge. Then we went into a small restaurant for some pizza.

The next morning, we went to the museum. We were going to walk there, but it started to rain so we took the metro. The museum was huge! There were paintings, old objects and even dinosaur bones. My favourite thing was the Statue of Liberty model in the entrance hall.

On the third day, the weather was perfect again. We went to Central Park, which is right in the middle of the city. We walked across the park to the lake and we had a picnic on the grass. Lots of families were there, and some children were riding bikes round the lake.

Before we left, we went to the post office to buy some stamps. We sent postcards to our friends and family at home. New York is going to be one of my favourite places in the world!

sections.title: Reading: The Road to Hope
sections.instructions: Read the poem-story about a family's journey to Hope, then answer the questions.
sections.passage:
I'm Kay and he's Jay, and we're both here today, to talk about our life in the USA. Our country is big and our country is wide, over two thousand miles from side to side.

Last year we went on a trip in the car. 'Don't worry,' said Mum, 'we aren't going to go far.' We wanted to visit this small town called Hope, where Grandma was born, she's called Ear-Ella Cope.

But the road was so long and it went on and on. Over bridge after bridge until Dad said, 'We're wrong. This isn't the way to Hope town, do you know, we shouldn't be going this way, no, no, no.'

Dad shouted, 'We should go back!' But Mum said, 'No, wait is best.' We sat in silence, and looked at Yvonne, who picked up the laptop and turned it on.

Our sister is small, so clever, so kind. Searched her laptop and tried hard to find. An app that would help us all get to the town. 'Go left,' she said now, 'and go up please, not down.'

We went left at the shops and straight on at the light. The day was so warm and the sun was so bright. 'Look!' said Yvonne, 'Can you all see the sign?' I'm quite good at finding directions online.'

We laughed and we laughed and said, 'Well done, Yvonne. We're here at the town, and we didn't go wrong.' From now on it's your job to show us the way. Thank you for helping us get here today.'
